record.context_brief: PTA gravitational waves and enhanced ALP-density regions
record.original_question: In the ALP scenario where large closed domain walls with mass M > M_max separate wall-dominated regions from the surrounding Universe, how is the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by those domain walls, and how do the surrounding regions of enhanced ALP density evolve after the wall separates from the rest of the Universe?

evidence.quote: Large closed domain walls with mass M > Mmax separate the region of their dominance from the surrounding Universe. Formation of these walls is accompanied by gravitational wave background radiation, which can reproduce the PTA data [36].
The open questions in this scenario are generation of GW background from the domain walls and evolution of the regions of the enhanced ALP density.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cosmological scenario in which a real pseudoscalar field (an axion-like particle, ALP) admits a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-like discrete vacuum structure, leading to the formation of two-dimensional domain walls during the evolution of the early Universe. Suppose that, in addition to the usual scaling network, sufficiently large closed domain walls form, each enclosing a region whose ALP energy density exceeds the average cosmological energy density. Let $M$ denote the rest mass of such a closed wall (its surface tension integrated over its area at formation), and assume there exists a critical value $M_{\max}$ such that for $M > M_{\max}$ the closed wall encloses a region that, at some time, becomes wall-dominated and detaches dynamically from the surrounding Hubble flow.

Address the following two problems:

(a) Derive the stochastic gravitational-wave background produced by the population of such large closed domain walls. Specifically, compute the present-day spectral energy density $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ as a function of frequency $f$, in terms of the wall tension $\sigma$, the mass distribution of closed walls, the cosmic time of wall formation, and the dynamics governing each wall's collapse or oscillation, and determine under what parameter ranges this spectrum can reproduce the nano-hertz signal observed by pulsar timing arrays.

(b) Determine the post-detachment evolution of the regions of enhanced ALP density that are bounded by these large closed walls. In particular, describe how such a region's energy density, size, and gravitational dynamics evolve after it separates from the cosmological expansion of the surrounding Universe, and characterize the resulting compact objects (e.g., axion stars, primordial black holes, or ALP miniclusters) that may form, including their mass function and abundance.
artifact.category_tag: Cosmological domain walls and gravitational waves
artifact.status_search_result: The two questions—precise computation of the stochastic GW background from large closed ALP domain walls and the post-detachment evolution of enhanced ALP-density regions—remain active research problems. Recent works (2023–2026) study GW signals from axionic domain walls at PTA frequencies including QCD bias, particle friction, and level crossing, and discuss formation of primordial black holes / axion miniclusters from collapsing walls, but no fully settled, model-independent treatment exists. The status is therefore open.

status_evidence.title: Axionic domain walls at Pulsar Timing Arrays: QCD bias and particle friction
status_evidence.snippet: Friction from Standard Model particles can play a significant role in ALP domain walls whose GW signal peaks at PTA frequencies.
status_evidence.claim: GW background from ALP domain walls relevant to PTA is still being modeled and is sensitive to friction and bias terms.

status_evidence.title: Gravitational waves and primordial black holes from axion domain walls in level crossing
status_evidence.snippet: Studies GW emission and PBH formation from collapsing axion domain walls.
status_evidence.claim: Post-collapse evolution of dense regions bounded by axion walls (PBHs/miniclusters) is an active research topic.

status_evidence.title: Gravitational waves from the axiverse
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2026) analysis of GW signals from axion-like domain wall networks.
status_evidence.claim: GW spectra from ALP wall networks continue to be refined in 2026 literature.
